=== Project 54445 and 59142 Crusoe Comments to Review of ERCOT Interconnection for Large Loads.pdf ===
                                        PROJECT NO. 54445


 REVIEW OF PROTOCOLS ADOPTED                        §    PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
 BY     THE      INDEPENDENT                        §
                                                                      OF TEXAS
 ORGANIZATION                                       §

                                        PROJECT NO. 59142


 REVIEW      OF                  ERCOT’S            §    PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
 INTERCONNECTION               PROCESSES            §
                                                                      OF TEXAS
 FOR LARGE LOADS                                    §

 CRUSOE TECHNOLOGIES, LLC’S COMMENTS ON RECOMMENDED APPROVAL
           OF PGRR 145 BY THE ERCOT BOARD OF DIRECTORS


         Crusoe Technologies, LLC (“Crusoe”) respectfully submits these comments to Project No.

54445 (Review of Protocols Adopted by the Independent Organization) and Project No. 59142

(Review of ERCOT Interconnection Process for Large Loads).


                                   I.      INTRODUCTION

         Crusoe respectfully requests that the Commission provide formal guidance, by the June 18

Open Meeting, on the refund requirements that should apply to financial commitments that an

Interconnecting Large Load Entity (“ILLE”) makes to be included in Batch Zero. There is

currently a regulatory gap regarding refund requirements for financial security required for Large

Loads to be included in Batch Zero because refund provisions are not included in PGRR 145. Clear

direction from the Commission is needed regarding the refund requirements that should apply to

Batch Zero financial commitments, so that such direction can be incorporated into the agreements

that are currently being negotiated between an ILLE and its Interconnecting Transmission Service

Provider (“TSP”) and/or Interconnecting Distribution Service Provider (“DSP”). Additionally,

Crusoe respectfully requests that the Commission provide guidance establishing that an ILLE may

                                                1
HB: 4917-8223-4804.3
 satisfy site control requirements in PGRR 145 by identifying that the applicable property interest

is held by the ILLE’s parent company or affiliate; such guidance would reflect the commercial

reality that often an ILLE’s affiliate, not the ILLE itself, holds the deed, lease, or other property

interest for the site where a large load facility will be located.

         Time is of the essence, since an ILLE is required to execute the relevant agreements and

make Batch Zero qualification submissions by June 26 if the ILLE’s Interconnecting TSP or

Interconnecting DSP is Oncor Electric Delivery Company (“Oncor”) or by July 10 (which is the

deadline provided in PGRR 145).


        II.       REQUESTED GUIDANCE ON REFUNDABILITY OF BATCH ZERO

                                         FINANCIAL SECURITY

         There are currently no requirements regarding refundability for the financial security that

ILLEs must pay to be included in Batch Zero, which will be multimillion-dollar financial

commitments for many large load developers. As requested by Commission Staff, ERCOT

removed the refund provisions from PGRR 145, so PGRR 145 does not identify whether or how

an Interconnecting TSP or Interconnecting DSP must refund financial commitments that an ILLE

makes to be included in Batch Zero.

         Separately, the Commission has a Proposal for Publication in Project No. 58481 that would

set forth financial security requirements and refundability terms that the PUCT anticipates will be

adopted in September 2026. However, it is unclear how the Commission’s forthcoming rule would

affect the Batch Zero financial security contracts that must be executed by July 10 th. This

regulatory uncertainty means that ILLEs must execute agreements and make multimillion-dollar




                                                   2
HB: 4917-8223-4804.3
 financial security payments to their Interconnecting TSP or Interconnecting DSP while having no

idea what the terms are regarding when and how that financial security could be refunded.

         On April 29, 2026, Commission Staff filed a memo in Project No. 59142 that provided

recommended guidance on how refunds should be handled for Batch Zero financial commitments. 1

Staff recommended the following refundability criteria for Batch Zero:

        Up to 100% refund of Batch Zero financial security for an ILLE seeking Batch Zero base
         load status under Planning Guide § 9.2.1.1(1)(e)

        Up to 50% refund of Batch Zero financial security for an ILLE seeking Batch Zero base
         load status under Planning Guide § 9.2.1.1(1)(f)

        Up to 80% refund of Batch Zero financial security for an ILLE seeking Batch Zero
         studied load status under Planning Guide § 9.2.1.2


         In general, Crusoe supports Staff’s recommendations regarding the refundability of

financial security in Batch Zero, although Crusoe would recommend that a large load seeking

studied load status be able to obtain a refund of up to 100%, since a studied load has no guaranteed

MW allocation (unlike a base load) and thus does not benefit from the advance certainty that it

will receive a certain MW allocation in Batch Zero when it makes the required financial

commitments.

         However, while Staff’s memo provides helpful clarifications, more formal and

comprehensive direction from the Commission is needed in order to provide clarity and certainty

to large load developers that are now in the process of entering into agreements with TSPs and




      1
        See Project No. 59142 (Review of ERCOT Interconnection Process for Large Loads), Staff’s April 29, 2026
Comments on PGRR 145 at 2-3 (April 29, 2026).


                                                      3
HB: 4917-8223-4804.3
 DSPs related to financial security commitments for Batch Zero. Crusoe further respectfully

requests that the Commission clarify that the forthcoming Project No. 58481 rule would not

retroactively apply to the Batch Zero financial security agreements executed prior to the effective

date of that rule. Crusoe respectfully requests that the Commission provide this guidance at its

June 18 Open Meeting so that there is time to incorporate the Commission’s refund guidance into

agreements that are being executed to meet Batch Zero requirements by the July 10 deadline in

PGRR 145 or the June 26 deadline set by Oncor.

         Formal guidance from the Commission is needed for several reasons. First, Commission

Staff’s guidance is helpful, but it does not constitute formal guidance from the Chair and

Commissioners, and so far the draft Batch Zero financial security agreements from TSPs or DSPs

do not incorporate Staff’s guidance on refundability. Additionally, further guidance is needed as

soon as possible on the criteria that an ILLE must satisfy in order to receive a refund, and the

timing of refunds. By expanding on the type of guidance provided in the April 29 memo, the

Commission can provide a more comprehensive framework on refundability of financial security

required for Batch Zero large load projects.


         It is especially important for the Commission to clarify the timing and requirements for

obtaining a refund because a financial institution issuing a letter of credit requires a defined return

event as a condition of credit approval. Without clear terms governing the refundability of financial

security in Batch Zero agreements, a lender cannot properly underwrite the credit exposure, which

may cause material delays in an ILLE’s ability to obtain a letter of credit from a financial institution

so that the ILLE can satisfy the financial commitment requirements for Batch Zero. This may

jeopardize the ILLE’s ability to meet Batch Zero qualification deadlines.




                                                   4
HB: 4917-8223-4804.3
          Crusoe recommends that the Commission issue a memorandum that provides guidance on
the following issues:

        Confirm Commission support for the refund percentages provided in Staff’s April 29
         memo for large loads that seek to qualify as base load under Planning Guide Section
         9.2.1.1(1)(e)-(f).


        Provide guidance that a large load that qualifies as studied load under Planning Guide
         Section 9.2.1.2 should be eligible for a refund of up to 100% rather than 80% because a
         studied load, unlike a base load, is not guaranteed to receive its requested MW allocation
         in Batch Zero.

        Establish clear criteria for the refundability terms of the Batch Zero financial security.

        Establish a timeline for when and how an Interconnecting TSP or DSP must refund Batch
         Zero financial security, including in scenarios where the ILLE withdraws the
         interconnection request, does not utilize the full requested capacity, or is not allocated its
         full requested capacity. Establish criteria for how such refunds should be handled.

        Confirm that an ILLE should receive a full refund of any financial security that is tied to
         any requested MWs that cannot be served by the ERCOT grid, as determined in the Batch
         Zero Interconnection Study.

        Confirm that an ILLE should receive a full refund of financial security if ERCOT
         determines that the customer’s project does not qualify for inclusion in Batch Zero.

        Confirm that an ILLE should receive a full refund of CIAC if the large load customer
         provided CIAC for inclusion in Batch Zero as base load, but the customer ultimately
         qualifies to be studied load (which does not require posting of CIAC).

        Clarify that Batch Zero financial security would be applied to meet financial security
         requirements that will be adopted for large load interconnection agreements in Project No.
         58481.
                       III.   REQUESTED GUIDANCE ON SITE CONTROL

         Crusoe also requests that the Commission provide further guidance interpreting the ILLE

site control requirements in PGRR 145. As written, PGRR 145 requires an ILLE to attest that the

ILLE holds one or more of the property interests that constitute an authorized method of site control

                                                   5
HB: 4917-8223-4804.3
 for Batch Zero purposes.2 However, from a commercial standpoint, this is often not how property

ownership interests are structured for large data center campuses. It is common for affiliate entities

of the ILLE—not the ILLE itself—to hold the relevant property interest for the parcel(s) of land

for each data center building. Typically, financing of these multibillion-dollar data center projects

requires that each specific entity that is financing that particular data center building hold the real

property interest in the land. Therefore, Crusoe respectfully requests that the Commission provide

formal guidance that an ILLE may satisfy the site control requirements in PGRR 145 if the ILLE

can provide documentary evidence that the relevant property interest (which otherwise satisfies

the applicable PGRR 145 requirements) is held by the ILLE’s parent company or affiliate.

         Crusoe supports Texas Industrial Energy Consumers’ (“TIEC”) comments that PGRR 145

should be interpreted to allow site control to be demonstrated through a property interest other than

a property interest held in the ILLE’s own name, and agrees with TIEC that the current PGRR 145

language permits such an interpretation.3 Crusoe concurs with TIEC that it is appropriate to allow

affiliate-held site control for large load customers, since this is equivalent to what is permitted for

generation interconnection in ERCOT, and because affiliate involvement is acceptable in other

contexts in PGRR 145, including in provisions that allow an ILLE to satisfy financial commitment

requirements through a corporate or parental guaranty. 4

         Crusoe also supports TIEC’s recommendation that the same approach should apply to long

lead time equipment, so that an ILLE may still satisfy long lead time equipment attestation

requirements if an entity other than the ILLE—such as an end-use customer or an affiliated entity


         2
           See PGRR 145, Board report, proposed Planning Guide § 9.2.1.1(1)(e)(viii), § 9.2.1.1(1)(f)(vi), and §
9.2.1.2(1)(b).
         3
        See Project No. 54445, Texas Industrial Energy Consumers’ Comments on Recommended Approval of
PGRR145 by ERCOT Board of Directors at 2 (June 11, 2026) (hereinafter “TIEC Comments”).
         4
             See id. at 3.


                                                       6
HB: 4917-8223-4804.3
 acting on the project’s behalf—has ordered equipment with a lead time of at least 18 months and

the equipment is committed for installation at the project site. 5 Crusoe agrees it would be

appropriate, as TIEC has suggested, for the Commission to “clarify that this language is intended

to apply not only in the context of affiliated entities within the same corporate family—for

example, a subsidiary securing equipment on behalf of its parent, or vice versa—but also where a

tenant secures the equipment for the ILLE developer, or a developer secures the equipment for an

ILLE tenant.”6

                                    IV.    CONCLUSION

         Crusoe appreciates the Commission’s consideration of these comments. Again, since time

is of the essence, Crusoe recommends that the Commission provide the necessary guidance by

June 18, so that the Commission’s guidance can be incorporated into agreements governing Batch

Zero financial commitments ahead of the June 26 (Oncor) and July 10 (PGRR 145) deadlines. This

guidance will provide important clarity to developers who are in the process of making

multimillion-dollar financial commitments to develop major projects in Texas.




Dated: June 12, 2026

 REVIEW       OF       ERCOT’S                                §      PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
 INTERCONNECTION PROCESSES FOR                                §
                                                                                   OF TEXAS
 LARGE LOADS                                                  §

          EXECUTIVE SUMMARY OF CRUSOE TECHNOLOGIES LLC’S COMMENTS


    •    Crusoe requests that the Commission provide formal guidance on how refunds should be addressed
         for Batch Zero financial commitments. The Commission’s guidance should address the criteria
         required for an ILLE to obtain a refund, as well as the timing and process for the Interconnecting
         TSP or Interconnecting DSP to provide the refund.

    •    The Commission’s guidance should also address:
                o      The refund required when an ILLE does not receive its full requested capacity in the Batch
                       Zero Interconnection Study, which should be 100% for any financial security posted for
                       requested MWs that were not allocated to the ILLE; and
                o      The refund of CIAC that an ILLE posted for base load qualification when a large load
                       later qualifies as studied load in Batch Zero. Since CIAC is only required for base load,
                       an ILLE should receive a full refund of CIAC if the ILLE only qualifies as studied load.

    •    The Commission should clarify that financial commitments made in Batch Zero will be applied to
         fund the financial commitments required for an interconnection agreement under 16 TAC § 25.194.


    •    The Commission should provide guidance that an ILLE can satisfy PGRR 145 site control
         requirements by demonstrating that a relevant property interest is held by the ILLE’s affiliate or
         parent company.


    •    The Commission should provide guidance that an ILLE can satisfy PGRR 145 long lead time
         equipment requirements by attesting that the ILLE’s affiliate or end-use customer has ordered
         equipment with a lead time of at least 18 months.
